-75.67320,39.68600.name: Delaware Institute for Reproductive Medicine, PA
-75.67320,39.68600.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Jeffrey B. Russell, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-113.75121,52.45395.name: Lacombe Research and Development Centre
-113.75121,52.45395.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, November 2023
-113.75121,52.45395.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, November 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-57.57149,-38.04587.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: http://www.halitus.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-47.88280,-15.79390.name: CTNBio — national biosafety commission
-47.88280,-15.79390.desc: Brazil’s biosafety commission, which approves engineered organisms for a country planting more than fifty million hectares of them. Its decisions are published and its meetings minuted, making it one of the more legible regulators in the world. It has also approved essentially everything put in front of it, including engineered eucalyptus and, in 2018, the first engineered insect approved for unrestricted commercial release anywhere.

-121.98800,37.54800.name: Cyagen
-121.98800,37.54800.desc: A contract company producing custom engineered mice and cell lines to order, with operations in the United States and China. The service model means a laboratory anywhere can commission an animal without holding the capability itself — the animals exist, the work is contracted, and the resulting lines often appear in no public catalogue.

-121.98800,37.54800.name: Perfect Day
-121.98800,37.54800.desc: Makes dairy proteins by fermenting engineered fungi, sold in products that require no GMO labelling because the organism is not in the final food. It is a substantial route by which engineering enters food while staying outside every labelling argument.
